# Williams Companies Internship 2027–2028: Programs, Deadlines & How to Apply


*Last updated: August 2026*


Williams Companies posts its University Internship applications every mid-August and closes the window about six weeks later, at the end of September, so if you're reading this in the back half of August 2026, the summer 2027 window covering Engineering, Business, and IT tracks may already be live on Williams's Workday board. For the 2027–2028 cycle (you apply during 2026, you intern in summer 2027), that's roughly nine months before the June start. Williams also has a real number behind the pitch: 79% of its 2022 intern class of 50 converted into full-time roles. Miss the six-week window and the next shot is next August.

## What Is a Williams Companies Internship?


A Williams Companies internship is a paid, 10-to-12-week summer placement inside one of three tracks (Engineering, Business, or IT) at the Tulsa, Oklahoma energy infrastructure company (NYSE: WMB), Fortune 500 #373 in 2026. Williams operates more than 32,000 miles of pipeline across 24 states, including the Transco system that alone carries an estimated 15% of the natural gas used in the US; company-wide, Williams says its network handles close to a third of the country's gas. Interns work out of Tulsa, Houston, Pittsburgh, or Salt Lake City. Williams converted 79% of its 50-person 2022 intern class into full-time hires, and[Glassdoor gives the company a 3.8-out-of-5 overall rating](https://www.glassdoor.com/Overview/Working-at-Williams-EI_IE736.11,19.htm) across 684 reviews, with a 5-out-of-5 intern rating, though that intern figure rests on only 5 reviews.


## When Do Williams Companies Internship Applications Open for 2027–2028?


Williams's calendar is documented and consistent year over year: University Internship applications for Engineering, Business, and IT post in mid-August and close about six weeks later, at the end of September, with campus interviews starting the day after each school's career fair and decisions landing within 1-2 weeks. So for summer 2027 you apply in fall 2026, roughly nine months before the June start. Williams also runs a separate Technical-School internship track (Aircraft Maintenance, Automotive, Corrosion, Diesel, Instrumentation & Controls, Natural Gas Compression, and Process Operations) that recruits on its own calendar starting mid-February, so check both tracks if either fits you.

### Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open


Williams doesn't run open-ended rolling review, but the mechanics push the same direction. Campus interviews start the day after each school's career fair, so whichever schools go first get seen first, and decisions land within 1-2 weeks of the interview rather than dragging out. Combine that with a six-week posting window and a fixed signing-day deadline in late October, and a student who applies in week one is competing for a full slate of open seats. A student who applies in week five is competing for whatever the earlier interviews left behind.

## Which Williams Companies Internship Programs Should You Target?


Williams runs three university internship tracks (Engineering, Business, and IT), a separate Technical-School track, and a 1-year Early Career Program for new graduates. Start with your major: the tracks map directly to Williams's own recruiting list, and the interview panel screens against that track's specific job description.

Business Finance, accounting, economics, energy management, data analytics, or MBA; Tulsa or Houston 10-12 weeks Financial modeling, Excel, communication


IT MIS, computer science, BIS, or CIS; Tulsa or Houston 10-12 weeks SQL, data engineering, Power BI


Technical-School Internships Aircraft Maintenance, Automotive, Corrosion, Diesel, Instrumentation & Controls, Natural Gas Compression, and Process Operations 10-12 weeks Hands-on technical training; recruited spring and fall on a separate calendar

See the full track and major breakdown, including the separate Technical-School track and its mid-February posting window, on the[official careers page](https://www.williams.com/careers/) . The Early Career Program pulls primarily from the intern pool rather than posting as its own open search.


## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


Williams publishes the same core requirements across its University Internship postings:


• **Enrollment & majors:** current undergrad or grad student in an eligible major, Engineering (chemical, electrical, mechanical, civil, energy, environmental, or petroleum), Business (finance, accounting, economics, energy management, data analytics, or MBA), or IT (MIS, computer science, BIS, or CIS), expected to return to coursework after the summer.


• **GPA:** no minimum published anywhere on Williams's careers site or FAQ (see the nuance below).


• **Work authorization:** the 2026 Engineering posting states the role "is not eligible for sponsorship, OPT or CPT." If you need visa sponsorship, this internship path isn't available.


• **Relocation & driving:** must relocate for the full 10 to 12 weeks to Tulsa, Houston, Pittsburgh, or Salt Lake City; Engineering roles also require a valid state driver's license with a clean driving record.


### Does Williams Have a GPA Cutoff?


No published minimum, anywhere: not on the general careers FAQ, the Early Career Program page, or the University Internship page. That's a real gap, not an oversight. Williams told[NACE in 2023](https://www.naceweb.org/talent-acquisition/internships/williams-shifts-to-basing-intern-hiring-and-development-on-career-readiness-competencies) that it screens against career-readiness competencies (communication, critical thinking, leadership, professionalism, teamwork, and technology) rather than a hard number. What actually gates you: the no-sponsorship line rules out students who need a visa, and the relocation requirement rules out anyone who can't commit to Tulsa, Houston, Pittsburgh, or Salt Lake City for the full summer.


## What Skills Does Williams Companies Look For, and How Do You Build Them?


The fullest window into what Williams screens for is its 2026 Engineering internship posting, which asks for organizational and interpersonal skills, the ability to work independently and within a matrixed team, strong verbal and written communication, analytical and creative problem solving, Microsoft Office proficiency, leadership experience, and intellectual curiosity, on top of a safety-first mindset. A same-cycle Finance & Accounting posting confirms Williams runs the same competency-based screen across tracks, though its listing text was too short to analyze the same way. Every Williams internship posting is also tagged against a standard set of career-readiness competencies (communication, critical thinking, leadership, professionalism, teamwork, technology) rather than a role-specific skill list.

## What Is the Williams Companies Application and Interview Process Like?


Williams runs a shorter funnel than a Wall Street bank, built around campus recruiting rather than months of open review:


1. **Apply through[Williams's Workday board](https://williams.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/External)** , linked from[williams.com/careers](https://www.williams.com/careers/) , choosing one of the Engineering, Business, or IT tracks.


2. **Self-recorded video screen.** Williams says candidates "may be asked to complete a brief self-recorded virtual interview" to help narrow the pool before live interviews.


3. **Panel interview.** Top candidates interview in person, often the day after their school's career fair, or virtually if that's not practical. Come ready for behavioral, STAR-format questions.


4. **Decision and signing day.** Williams says it aims to decide within a week to ten days of the interview, and the formal offer-acceptance deadline is the last Thursday or Friday of October, marked with an on-campus signing-day tradition.


Across all Williams roles, not intern-specific,[Glassdoor logs 145 interviews](https://www.glassdoor.com/Interview/Williams-Interview-Questions-E736.htm) at an average difficulty of 2.8 out of 5, with 69% rating the experience positive. Rehearse the behavioral round: our[HireVue question guide with a free AI mock tool](https://www.extern.com/post/hirevue-interview-questions-2025-free-ai-mock-tool) runs the same self-recorded-video format Williams uses to screen.

## How Do You Stand Out for a Williams Internship?


Three moves, all doable before the window even opens. First, apply in week one of the six-week posting period. Second, build proof in Williams's own language: real-time data analysis, financial modeling, or a finished engineering-adjacent project speaks louder than a GPA the company doesn't publish anyway. Third, treat the interview as an audition for the year after. Williams converted 79% of its 2022 intern class of 50 into full-time hires, largely through its 1-year Early Career Program, so recruiters are already picturing you in that seat. Show up with a project you can describe in STAR format, since that's the interview style Williams tells candidates to expect.

## FAQ


### Can I still apply for a summer 2026 Williams Companies internship?


Not through the general path. The only live summer-2026-linked posting is a Return Engineering Intern role restricted to students who already interned with Williams, and it closed August 5, 2026. New applicants should target summer 2027: postings follow Williams's mid-August pattern, so check the Workday board now.


### When do Williams Companies internship applications open for summer 2027?


Based on Williams's documented pattern, expect mid-August 2026, with the window closing about six weeks later at the end of September. That's roughly nine months before the June 2027 start, and if you're reading this in late August, the window may already be live.


### Is Williams Companies internship recruiting rolling?


Not fully rolling. Williams keeps a fixed, roughly six-week posting window, but campus interviews start the day after each school's career fair, so earlier fairs get first access to interview slots and decisions land within 1-2 weeks.


### Does Williams require a minimum GPA for internships?


No minimum is published anywhere on the careers site or FAQ. Williams says it screens against career-readiness competencies (communication, critical thinking, leadership, teamwork, technology) instead. The real gates are the no-sponsorship rule and the relocation requirement.


### What is the Williams Companies internship interview process like?


Apply through Workday, complete a brief self-recorded video screen, then interview with a panel, often the day after your school's career fair. Williams says it decides within a week to ten days, with a formal offer-acceptance deadline the last Thursday or Friday of October.


### Do Williams interns get return offers?


Williams's own HR team told NACE that 79% of its 2022 intern class of 50 converted to full-time roles. That's a single historical data point, not an annually published rate, but it's a real, attributed number few peer pages can cite.


### What skills does Williams look for in interns?


Its 2026 Engineering posting asks for written and verbal communication, analytical and creative problem solving, organizational and interpersonal skills, matrixed teamwork, leadership experience, Microsoft Office proficiency, real-time data analysis, and a safety-first mindset.


### How much does a Williams Companies internship pay?


Williams pays hourly, tiered by expected graduation date. The 2026 Return Engineering posting listed $33.70/hour for the Summer 2029 tier up to $47.60/hour for the Master's-program tier, plus a $2,500 housing stipend and relocation help for moves over 50 miles.


The window is about six weeks, and the interview process moves fast once your school's career fair passes. Spend the runway before it building proof: a[remote Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships) turns "interested in energy infrastructure" into a finished project a Workday application can point to.
